A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skyfall-GS and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D. Content can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original DFC2019 and GoogleEarth experiments, component ablations, two user studies with 44 participants each, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds curriculum-direction, single-pass refinement, reprojection, boundary-coverage, and cross-view consistency results.

M1.justification: The reconstruction components, FlowEdit/FLUX refinement, curriculum, multi-sample training, losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Reverse-curriculum and single-pass variants are additional experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DFC2019 and GoogleEarth scenes, additional Jacksonville AOIs, historical landmarks, bridges, and merged JAX_214/JAX_260 region. The added checks reuse this coverage with different measurements and controls.

E2.justification: V4 adds single-pass diffusion and reverse-curriculum controls and compares the merged model against individual AOI models. The external comparator sets in the main benchmarks remain unchanged; the new EO-NeRF runtime mention is attributed information, not a newly evaluated image-quality baseline.

E3.justification: V4 substantially expands the validation design with a 62-view satellite reprojection evaluation, consecutive-frame DINOv2 cosine dissimilarity on a 17-degree orbit, a reported compute-matched single-pass comparison, reversed curriculum, and boundary-orbit comparisons. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The reprojection split is unclear: the prose says held-out views, while Table 10 calls them input views and its count equals the training-image total in Table 5.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether curriculum direction matters, iteration improves over one-pass refinement, diffusion preserves satellite fidelity, merging improves boundary coverage, and multiple samples improve temporal consistency (Tables 4, 10, 12 and Appendix D). These substantially strengthen the examination of central mechanisms and robustness claims beyond v2's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain qualitative random-seed diversity examples and report point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests. V4 does not introduce repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures; diffusion samples per view remain a method setting.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include reverse-curriculum FIDCLIP/CMMD of 53.03/4.170, single-pass 51.46/4.160 versus iterative 28.35/2.875, boundary-orbit comparisons, and consistency scores of 0.0340 versus 0.0264. New Table 10 reports 29.67/0.934/0.129 for Skyfall-GS versus 29.24/0.936/0.121 for Mip-Splatting: only PSNR is better. Retained benchmark scores are unchanged, but Table 1's aggregate DFC2019 pixel-metric entries disappear while the existing per-scene results remain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, projection assumptions, and RPC-to-perspective discussion are retained. The added cosine-dissimilarity measurement is an empirical evaluation metric, without new theoretical claims, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims the first demonstration of paired opacity regularization and pseudo-camera depth supervision in the satellite setting, and foregrounds curriculum plus multi-sample consensus. This refines the contribution positioning; the abstract and central satellite-only urban-synthesis claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Where v2 mentions artifacts at extreme street-level views, v4 explicitly excludes facade-close pedestrian-level synthesis below 10 degrees, citing transient objects and unreliable low-elevation references. It also interprets limited prompt steerability as a deliberate fidelity trade-off and adds explanations connecting the new controls to iterative refinement and satellite anchoring.

D1.justification: Appendix B's implementation details and access disclosures are unchanged. V4 specifies DINOv2 ViT-L/14 for the new consistency measurement and adds a locally measured Mip-Splatting runtime. However, v2's approximately 30-minute refinement, 32-minute update, and 4-second rendering breakdown is absent despite v4 directing readers to the supplement for it.

R1.justification: V4 adds VBench and DINOv2 references for the consistency evaluation and sharpens novelty positioning around satellite-specific component integration. The existing related-work discussion and cited research are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The contribution list, quantitative-comparison discussion, efficiency paragraph, conclusion, and limitations receive localized rewrites, with additional analytical paragraphs in the supplement. The overall section organization and most explanatory text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a substantially more compact page format and smaller margins throughout. Tables 1–2 are redesigned, Table 4 gains a row, Tables 10 and 12 are added, and existing figures and tables are repositioned. The existing 23 figures are retained; the narrower first-page margin also causes the arXiv stamp to overlap Figure 1's caption.

improvement.justification: The directional and single-pass controls in Tables 4 and 12 provide useful evidence for the refinement strategy, while the explicit pedestrian-level boundary clarifies applicability. These yield a modest overall improvement. The gain is limited by unclear reprojection holdout status, the claim of matching or exceeding Mip-Splatting despite worse SSIM and LPIPS in Table 10, and the lost timing breakdown.
